stories.title: The True Defensive Bugaboo
stories.summary:
TEXANS



	Red Zone: 4/5



	4th Down: 2/2



	 



	LIONS 



	Red Zone: 3/4



	4th Down: 2/2



	 



	CHARGERS 



	Red Zone: 1/4



	4th Down: 0/1



	 



	PATRIOTS



	Red Zone: 3/3



	4th Down: 2/2



	 



	RAMS



	Red Zone: 5/5



	4th Down: 2/2



	 



	Through 4 games:



	Opponents have score a TD in the red zone 76% of the time: 16/21, good for 27th in the league. Doesn’t matter if the opposing offense was previously struggling in that area, the Bills defense is the cure all.



	 



	Opponents have converted 4th downs 88% of the time: 8/9, good for 29th in the league.



	 



	These numbers HAVE to start regressing to the mean at some point. The Bills can’t be this putrid against every contender, can they? If those numbers can get to at least middle of the pack, I’d wager we all would feel very different about Jim Leonhard and his defense.

stories.title: Davison Igbinosun Starts Over Maxwell Hairston
stories.summary:
One of the things I found very interesting about last night's game was that after all the "tire pumping" the coaches did for Hairston throughout the week by talking about how we'd be needing him and leaning on him... they straight up switched him out for IGB.



	 



	And it was a lot more than just "you're sitting for a bit as a punishment for your behavior post game last week". If that were the case, after a couple series or maybe a quarter or so, he'd have switched with IGB.



	 



	Instead, Davison Igbinosun played on 84% of the snaps on Defense and Maxwell Hairston played just 21% of them. That's a total and complete role reversal between what Hairston and IGB were doing to that point with Benford on the field:



	 



	



	The Defense as a whole had issues last night (as is the norm this year). But lining up against those WR's in your first ever start in your 5th ever game - I thought he performed admirably.



	 



	It will be interesting to see if this trend continues going forward. From what we've seen out of both guys, I think the switch is the right call. And it's interesting to me that Leonhard or Brady made that switch so quickly.

stories.title: Hey, I just looked outside. The sky isn't falling. We are 4-1
stories.summary:
Look, I will admit right off the bat that it hasn't been pretty the last 3 weeks and the defense has been horrible throughout most of the 5 games. 



	 



	But we are 4-1. I'm pretty sure at the beginning of the year if we were told that would be the case we would have jumped on that. And we are tied as the #1 scoring offense in the NFL. And that's been by and large without DJ Moore who changes everything when he is out there. 



	 



	I will freely admit our defense is terrible outside the DL. But we are still stacking wins. 



	 



	Sure, it's ugly at times. And there is a LOT of work to do on defense especially. But there's a lot to like on this team right now as well. We have a good DL. Two full fledged stars there in Groot and Walker. And Carter is right behind them. Benford actually looked better last night and, considering the assignment, IGB played well I thought. 



	 



	It's October. Just keep stacking wins. Find a way to contain Bowers next week and 5-1 heading in to the bye is attainable.

stories.title: Horns up, horns down for Buffalo Bills vs. Los Angeles Rams
I'm out on Terell Bernard, Dorian Williams, and CJGJ
stories.summary:
I've seen enough of these 3 football players. All 3 of them are awful and need to be replaced on this defense ASAP. Last year Cole Bishop looked like a Safety on the rise with old man Jordan Poyer next to him being a declining but steady football player. I think a lot of Bishop's regression is he has Johnson next to him. Johnson has made one play this year and has been awful on every other play this year. 



	 



	Dorian Williams will have one good game and then he is absolutely atrocious for 2-3 other games. Bernard has more moments than Williams but he's injury prone, small, and not very athletic. Get Shaq Thompson and KEO ready to play cause I'm tired of watching them. 



	 



	I can live with Igbinosun and Hairston making mistakes because they are young players getting first time significant playing time and they will learn and hopefully get better as the season and years go by. 



	 



	While we're at it, I want Ed Oliver off this roster next year. Good player when he's on the field but he's never available. At this point he's flat out stealing money from the Bills organization.



	 



	As most of you know I'm a pretty level headed poster, I try to dig down below the surface to see what this organization is trying to achieve but I had to rant about this. Replacing those 3 players would go a long long way to making this defense better. 



	 



	Good Win, Go Bills.

stories.title: We Won. The Question is How with this D?
stories.summary:
Why is it the Bills Defense can't make a stop? I'd even settle for the Rams getting a field goal. Ironically, the oy stop we made was their FG Kicker misding a FG.



	 



	When it matters, 4th quarter, up by 7,  3rd and 5 near our end zone, the last minute of a game, or a close game, the Bills can't get a stop! It's not even close. Not one meaningful stop the last half of the game. Not one!



	 



	The fact that the Bills were in this game is a miracle. The offense finally got going after a horrible first half, and we still put up 37 on the road with our non-existent receiving core and penalty-prone OL and WR's.



	 



	Yet, our weak-ass, Swiss cheese, crappy scheme, out-of-place, bad angle, poor tackling, and undersized Charmin D allowed play after play and score after score. The Rams marched down 3 straight times without any resemblance of fight by this D. Then, we couldn't stop them in OT when Cook almost fumbled away the game!



	 



	Please...make a stop on D !



	 



	And, stop with the penalties too!



	 



	I know I am throwing a temper tantrum in a win, but there are literally red flag warnings all over this D, our scheme,  and the inability for this team to execute consistently.



	 



	Please at the trade deadline...follow this advice, Bills Front Office.

stories.title: The Beane Era Needs To End
stories.summary: Something about this game has pushed my tolerance level of Beane over the edge.  This game looked like Josh Allen against the Rams.  The defense was Swiss Cheese the entire night, and the Rams man coverage blanketed our receivers for much of the game - forcing Josh to put on his cape and make some crazy plays with his legs.  Yes, we won, but it was like a nightmarish repeat of everything this team does that comes up short when the playoffs come around.  At the end of the 4th Quarter, how many of you were yelling at the screen - "Just let them score so we have 40 seconds left."  That's not a good way to think about the team's defense.  😆  I hope it's something to do with the coaching, but I'm seeing a lot of gaps in talent on this team.  A lot.  And it feels like Beane has made some more whiffs on picks.
